contributions.statement: Keep acceptance validators the agent never sees, and make them vary data scale, boundary parameters, input order and alternate execution paths rather than replaying the visible fixture; agents that score ~97% on visible tests pass these validators less than half the time.
contributions.evidence: §4.1 construction (hidden validators vary scale/boundaries/ordering, inter-module contract tests); Table 2 and §8: Claude-Opus-5 96.64% public score vs 47.90% Pass@1; public 93-100% vs Pass@1 14-48% across eight model+harness configurations. Single attempt, no variance; Python scientific repos, so transfer to Java is indirect.
relative_to: held-out acceptance tests / patch overfitting in automated program repair

contributions.statement: Supplying extra domain rationale to an agent can lower exact success for a strong model while helping a weak one, so domain docs should be targeted and paired with executable checks rather than dumped into context.
contributions.evidence: §6.2 Figs. 6-7, 91-task subset: GPT-5.6-sol Pass@1 36.26% -> 31.87% with info (8 gained, 12 lost); DeepSeek-V4-flash 16.48% -> 23.08%. Two models, authors say not significant.
relative_to: more context is not better / context rot

reason: The visible-vs-hidden gap is large, measured across eight configurations, and gives a concrete recipe for what held-out validators should perturb. The domain-knowledge ablation is descriptive only.
